blocks.text: Neon Ooze is an aesthetic that developed in the 80s and 90s and was used most commonly for targeting children through gross-out marketing. The driving visual element were fluids such as slime, goop or toxic waste, with other related elements often thrown in such as nuclear, mad science or "creepy crawly" imagery. It reflects an era's playful obsession with eco-anxiety and gross-out humor.
Neon Ooze originated in the last 1980s, partly from real-world worries about toxic waste disposal and pollution of the time.
Themes: Mutant powers, toxic spills, mad scientists, and industrial waste.
Slime and Sludge: Dripping fluid, globs, melting shapes, and blobs.
Hot pinks, day-glo greens, electric purples, and radioactive yellows.
